newsitem.title: USA: Lexington Corporate raises, spends capital.
newsitem.headline: Lexington Corporate raises, spends capital.

text.p: Lexington Corporate Properties Inc said Wednesday it raised about $31 million from the sale of notes and a merger involving an "unaffiliated partnership," and acquired three industrial properties for $27 million.

Lexington Corporate, a real estate investment trust, said in a release that its operating subsidiary sold $25 million in eight percent exchangeable secured notes to an institutional investor in a private placement.
In relation to the acquisition of the properties, the company said, the "unaffiliated partnership" merged into one of Lexington's subsidiary partnerships.

As a result of the merger, the Lexington partnership issued 480,000 partnership units exchangeable for Lexington common stock and entitled to distributions at the same dividend rate as the stock, the company said.

It said that at the time of the merger, the sole assets of the "unaffiliated partnership" were about $6 million cash from the prior sale of a property and the right to acquire the properties in a tax-free exchange.

T. Wilson Eglin, president of Lexington Corporate, told Reuters that the three transactions are all related to one another. He said Lexington purchased the industrial properties to "hold for investment" and that the capital from the merger and notes was used for "this investment of property."

The company said the properties, containing 761,200 square feet and located on 46.56 acres near Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, are subject to net-leases with Exel Logistics Inc, whose parent company is NFC Plc.
Lexington Corporate said the notes require interest only payments at 8 percent per annum and are secured by first mortgage liens on the newly acquired properties.
The notes will be guaranteed by Lexington, and may be exchanged for Lexington common stock at $13 per share beginning in the year 2000, subject to adjustment, the company said.
The notes are subordinated to Lexington's revolving credit facility, the company added.
